# Color and brand

For any named brand, logo, brand kit or requested brand match, and for color contrast.

## Core

- Real brand facts win over inferred treatment. Use the selected snapshot's
  palette, type and supplied logo files, unmodified and in their documented
  variants.
- Exceptions are recorded, not improvised: they live in the brand snapshot's
  `overrides.md` or the active design direction.
- Say what was substituted or unavailable instead of claiming full brand
  fidelity, and name the kit used in the handoff.

## Using a kit

Read the project's brand snapshot (normally `brand/BRAND.md`, with `kit.json`
for tokens and the guides it links) as the `brand-kit` skill describes, and only
the fields the deliverable needs. Work for a website reads its site kit,
`brand/sites/<host>/kit.md`: take colours from `palette.json`, load the faces in
`fonts/` as local fonts, and place logos from `logos/` in the variant `kit.md`
marks transparent.

## Logos and marks

Inspect a logo file before placing it: pick the variant that suits the ground.
Verify a downloaded official mark against its published hash when one is given.
Partner and platform marks are sourced separately and never replace the user's
own brand as the design's identity.

## Color and contrast

A gradient word must stay readable at every stop; on
a dark ground, end on the lightest accent, never on dark purple, navy or black.

## After compression

Judge color in the encoded file, not the composition: faint decoration (glows,
patterns, watermark shapes) can vanish once encoded.

# Locate and safe areas

For placing labels, callouts and boxes on real images or moving subjects, and platform safe areas.

## Core

- Keep essential text and marks inside the platform's safe area (the `make-ai-video` skill's `references/social-safe-areas.md` lists them).

## Locate before you annotate

- **Segment it.** `voyager media cutout FRAME --prompt "the red car" --output
  located.png` (SAM 3, metered, about half a cent) keeps every confident match,
  so name exactly one instance ("the left-most car"). Then `voyager media
  crop-alpha located.png --output crop.png --json` reports its `box` (x, y,
  width, height in frame pixels) at no cost.

# Rights and delivery

For asset rights, credits, subtitles and delivery checks.

## Core

- Deliver a `CREDITS` file naming every third-party asset (samples, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence; credit on screen where a licence requires it; tell the user `CREDITS` lists the licences and the material is their responsibility.
- `voyager media review FILE` measures loudness but flags only a true peak above 0 dBTP (clipping): check `audio.integratedLUFS` near −14 and `audio.truePeakDBTP` at or below −1 yourself. It also checks black frames and duration. When the audio is a person's recording, review the processed voice stem (not the final mix with music) and pass the recording as `--audio-source`: review then flags a noise floor raised more than 15 dB or crushed dynamics; never force a very quiet recording to the target.
- To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use a video-understanding model with `voyager models run`; load `choose-media-model/references/understanding.md` for the paid upload route.

# Typography

For authoring text or changing fonts, layout or output size.

## Core

- Author exact words, numbers and supplied logos as controlled text or overlays;
  inspect the exported file rather than relying on generated imagery to spell.
- Write English copy in US spelling unless the user, their brand kit or the
  project uses another variety.
- Verify the actual renderer has the faces you use; a brand kit's supported-font
  flag is not proof of availability.
- Protect descenders,
  accents and cap height from clipping, including inside masks and line boxes.
- Use the editor integration skill for font loading. For a brand's fonts in Remotion or
  HyperFrames that is the generated brand-fonts helper, not hand-written `@font-face`;
  if it reports a substitute, say so to the user.
- Renderers add no motion blur: fine print and 1–2 px hairlines shimmer in fast moves; keep them out of fast moves or enlarge them.

# Delivery

## Bundled FFmpeg encoders

Voyager's bundled FFmpeg has no `libx264` or `libx265`. This applies to raw media
preparation and numbered-frame encoding as well as final delivery. Prefer
`voyager media assemble` for supported H.264 cuts/conversions: it selects the
platform encoder and reports when H.264 is unavailable. For raw FFmpeg, use the
encoder for the current platform:

| OS | Video arguments | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS | `-c:v h264_videotoolbox -q:v 85` | Constant quality, higher is better (Apple Silicon). On an Intel Mac use `-b:v 12M -allow_sw 1` |
| Windows | `-c:v h264_mf -b:v 12M` | Bitrate only |
| Linux | `-c:v libopenh264 -b:v 12M` | Only after a small probe encode succeeds; the encoder list alone does not prove Cisco's library is available. Otherwise deliver WebM or ask the person |

Inspect `ffmpeg -hide_banner -encoders`, then try a one-frame encode before
preparing the full media. On macOS, with a new output filename:

```sh
mkdir -p .voyager/tmp
ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -f lavfi -i color=size=128x128:rate=1 \
  -frames:v 1 -c:v h264_videotoolbox -q:v 85 -pix_fmt yuv420p .voyager/tmp/encoder-probe.mp4
```

## Platforms and website backgrounds

Drop audio with `-an` instead of shipping a silent track for a silent loop.
Platforms re-encode everything; smooth gradients band after that, so add fine
animated grain in the composition, or at encode with `-vf "noise=alls=3:allf=t"`.

## GIF and animated WebP

GIF frame delays are whole hundredths of a second, so use 20 or 25 fps (5 or
4 hundredths per frame); 30 fps rounds to an uneven speed, and browsers slow
delays under 2 hundredths down to 10, so never go above 50 fps. HyperFrames can
render one directly (`render --format gif --gif-loop 0 --fps 25`); from a master,
use a two-pass palette (`palettegen` then `paletteuse`), without dithering for flat
colors. The frame count must still be the loop length times the frame rate.
Animated WebP (`libwebp_anim`) is usually much smaller where the destination
accepts it.

## Size budgets

| Destination | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Chat and docs GIF (Slack, Notion, a deck) | ≤ 5 MB, ≤ 800 px wide |
| GitHub issue, PR or comment | ≤ 8 MB |
| Email | ≤ 1 MB, ≤ 600 px wide; some desktop Outlook versions show only the first frame, so that frame carries the message |
| Website background | ≤ 2–3 MB |
| Platform post | Encode for quality, not size |

# Loop mechanics

## Seam check

Run it on the master or the MP4, and on the GIF; the bundled FFmpeg cannot
decode animated WebP, so a WebP inherits its master's result. Compare the step
across the seam with a normal step inside the loop: read the file's real frame
count, extract its frames 0, 1 and last, and compare them with SSIM:

```sh
N=$(ffprobe -v error -count_frames -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=nb_read_frames -of default=nw=1:nk=1 loop.mp4)
if [[ ! "$N" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
  printf 'Cannot check seam: expected a positive frame count, got "%s" (N/A means unavailable).\n' "$N" >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p seam
ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -i loop.mp4 \
  -vf "select='eq(n\,0)+eq(n\,1)+eq(n\,$((N-1)))'" -fps_mode passthrough seam/f%d.png
ffmpeg -hide_banner -i seam/f3.png -i seam/f1.png -lavfi ssim -f null - 2>&1 | grep SSIM
ffmpeg -hide_banner -i seam/f1.png -i seam/f2.png -lavfi ssim -f null - 2>&1 | grep SSIM
```

`N` should equal the loop length times the frame rate (120 for 4 s at 30 fps,
100 for a 4 s GIF at 25 fps). `f1` is frame 0, `f2` frame 1 and `f3` the last
frame. Read the `All:` values, seam first:

- About equal to the inside step: seamless. A clean 4 s loop measured 0.9753
  against 0.9754 as MP4, and 0.9853 against 0.9853 as GIF.
- Clearly lower: a jump. A non-looping chart measured 0.900 against 0.989.
- Close to 1.0 and clearly above the inside step: the last frame repeats the
  first. The same loop with frame 0 appended measured 0.9986 against 0.9755
  (compression keeps a repeat from reading exactly 1.000).

## 3. Formats and safe areas

- **9:16**: keep the number, words and logo out of the platform's interface
  zones, as [social-safe-areas](../make-ai-video/references/social-safe-areas.md)
  lists them, and check with
  `voyager media review FILE --platform reels|shorts|tiktok --json`. There is no
  Stories zone in that check; check Stories separately against the placement's
  own guide, as that reference says.

For continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use [watch and listen](../choose-media-model/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).

## 4. Build

Build in the tool [make-motion-graphics](../make-motion-graphics/SKILL.md)
chooses. FFmpeg inspects the rendered file and makes the GIF and WebP encodes.

## 5. Deliver

Read [delivery](references/delivery.md) for encoding settings and size budgets
per destination: MP4 for platforms, GIF or animated WebP for chat, docs and
email, a small muted MP4 or WebM for web backgrounds.
